clinicalSummary: Three days of acute watery diarrhoea and vomiting; presented severely dehydrated and lethargic. Rehydration started but the child developed hypovolaemic shock and died in the resuscitation bay. Suspected infectious gastroenteritis — stool cultures pending.

Market vendor with sudden-onset profuse watery diarrhoea, muscle cramps and prostration. Brought in with profound dehydration and weak pulse; died despite IV fluids and antibiotics. Post-mortem rapid test positive for Vibrio cholerae.

Two weeks of stepwise fever, headache and abdominal pain treated at home. Admitted with peritonitis from a suspected ileal perforation; arrested during emergency laparotomy. Blood culture sent — typhoid strongly suspected clinically.

Severe chest pain for 6 hours with sweating and breathlessness. ECG showed inferior STEMI; developed ventricular fibrillation in the casualty department and could not be resuscitated. History of hypertension and smoking.
Elderly diabetic admitted with acute coronary syndrome complicated by pulmonary oedema. Deteriorated overnight despite diuresis and antiplatelets; cardiac arrest at 11:30, resuscitation unsuccessful.

Brought in dead after collapsing at work following sudden chest pain. No signs of trauma; known ischaemic heart disease. Certified dead on arrival — acute myocardial infarction recorded as probable cause.

High fever and confusion for 5 days, self-medicated at home. RDT positive; admitted with jaundice and oliguria consistent with severe malaria. Died of multi-organ failure on day 2 despite artesunate and supportive care.
Febrile convulsions and unresponsiveness overnight. Arrived comatose (GCS 6); falciparum parasitaemia confirmed on smear. Developed refractory seizures and died within 6 hours — cerebral malaria.

A week of intermittent fever, vomiting and severe anaemia (Hb 5.1). Transfused and started on IV artesunate but developed acute respiratory distress; died on day 3 of admission. Severe malaria with complications.

Admitted with lobar pneumonia and septic shock; COPD on home oxygen. Failed weaning trials and deteriorated over a week despite IV antibiotics and non-invasive ventilation. Died of respiratory failure.
Severe pneumonia with chest in-drawing and hypoxia on arrival; malnourished. Commenced on oxygen and IV antibiotics but progressed to respiratory failure overnight. Died on day 2 of admission.
Bilateral bronchopneumonia on chest X-ray with confusion and dehydration; COPD and heart failure comorbid. Treated for 6 days then arrested during a hypoxic episode — certified cause: pneumonia.
Tested SARS-CoV-2 positive on admission with bilateral COVID pneumonia; diabetic and hypertensive. Progressed to ARDS despite dexamethasone and oxygen therapy; died on day 9 of illness.
Respiratory distress and SpO2 78% on air; PCR confirmed COVID-19. Developed a secondary bacterial infection and sepsis on the ward. Died on day 6 of admission.
Frail nursing-home resident referred with COVID-19 pneumonia and dehydration. Comfort care instituted per family wishes; died peacefully on day 4. Cause certified as COVID-19 with frailty.

Admitted at 34 weeks with antepartum haemorrhage from placenta praevia; shocked on arrival. Emergency caesarean performed but mother arrested post-operatively from ongoing bleeding and DIC. Baby in NICU. MPDSR review initiated.

Admitted with severe pre-eclampsia at 37 weeks; developed eclamptic seizures in labour and progressed to HELLP syndrome. Died from intracerebral haemorrhage despite magnesium sulphate and caesarean delivery. MPDSR review initiated.

Stillborn at 38 weeks following reduced fetal movements for two days; mother a booked primigravida, delivery uncomplicated otherwise. Fresh stillbirth, no congenital abnormalities noted. Perinatal death review initiated.

Found unresponsive at home by neighbours; certified dead on arrival. No significant past medical history and no external injuries. Sudden unexplained death — post-mortem examination requested to establish cause.

Brought in by police after being found collapsed roadside with head injuries of undetermined mechanism — pedestrian versus vehicle suspected. Declared dead on arrival; case referred for forensic post-mortem.
